title: Chasing Papi
full_review:
Three women collide over the affections of a suave, hunky advertising executive who has deceived each into thinking that she is the only love of his life in the fatuous comedy "Chasing Papi" (Fox). This debut film by Linda Mendoza, though sporting an easy-to-look-at, up-and-coming Hispanic cast, is doomed by an inane script and flat, forced humor which ultimately proves to be about as appetizing as a three-day-old burrito.

Tomas Fuentes (Eduardo Verastegui) is handsome, intelligent and charming -- he is also on the verge of a nervous breakdown. The problem is, he is in love with three women, each safely separated by frequent-flyer miles, and blissfully ignorant of the amorous competition for their "Papi Chulo" -- a term of endearment in Latin culture meaning "my beautiful man."

First there is Lorena (Roselyn Sanchez), a Chicago lawyer whose blend of brains and beauty appeals to Tomas' sensitive, intellectual side. Behind door No. 2 is the Latin bombshell Cici (Sofia Vergara), a Charo-like Miami cocktail waitress whose curvaceous salsa physique satisfies his less cerebral needs. Then there's the New York heiress, Patricia (Jaci Velasquez), sophisticated and spoiled, who sees in Tomas an escape from her stifling Iberian blueblood mother.

Prompted by insecurity and the exhortations of famed television astrologer Walter Mercado -- whose televised horoscope readings seem tailor-made for each woman -- the three Latin lovelies chart courses for Los Angeles, each hoping to surprise Tomas. Yet not even his Don Juan good looks can help him charm his way out of trouble when, after showing up on his doorstep simultaneously and discovering they have been triple-timed, they descend on him like harpies. Ah, what tango-ed webs we weave!

Faced with the unenviable task of choosing one, Tomas passes out -- due in part to shock, and to the tranquilizers his doctor prescribed to treat his anxiety -- triggering a sequence of events which quickly cha-chas from the silly to the absurd. Along the way the filmmaker wedges a subplot into the story revolving around Cici's car and a bag of stolen money which serves no purpose beyond supplying pursuers from whom the women can flee in high heels.

Predictably, the competitors join forces to save their comatose Adonis, who -- mercifully for him -- remains unconscious through much of the film. However, in the end Tomas is left hung out to dry, as the women discover that the bond of friendship that has developed among them is more fulfilling than anything one man could offer them.

Very little of the narrative holds together and the film's strained dialogue and contrived plot devices amount to the worst Latin endeavor since the Bay of Pigs.

Due to some mild sexual humor, the USCCB Office for Film & Broadcasting classification is A-III -- adults. The Motion Picture Association of America rating is PG -- parental guidance suggested.
